Subject: Re: Edge PoP switch configs for private onboarding

Erin — thanks for sending these over. I pulled the attachments and kicked off an initial skim. We'll run our standard preflight + an additional edge-specific audit. High level checklist we'll cover:

- Verify VLAN tags and interface mapping align with your vlan-map PNG
- Confirm MTU set to 9000 across trunk ports for KV cache traffic (we'll flag mismatches)
- STP root consistency for the PoP; detect ports in tx-only state
- eBGP neighbor configs & AS-path sanity for the peering routers
- ACLs: ensure no broad 0.0.0.0/0 allow to tenant subnets; check for implicit permit rules
- Management plane: make sure out-of-band mgmt is on a dedicated VLAN and access lists restrict to OrthoWave IPs + Redwood bastion

Marissa, can you own the switch-config diff and run the simulated validation? Karthik, please confirm if we need any config-level changes for KMS-proxied traffic or encrypted egress. Ben — will need you on the maintenance window if we do a live BGP test.

Proposed maintenance window options:
- Tue 2028-09-19 01:00-02:00 UTC
- Wed 2028-09-20 22:00-23:00 UTC

I will upload our validation checklist to the MAP doc and share the link once ready.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Edge PoP switch configs for private onboarding

Adding the edge-level audit notes and exact commands we'll use for config validation. I'll run these against the provided file and send a redlined diff. Quick checklist + sample checks:

1) Interface mapping and VLANs  - Confirm trunk/untagged status for each interface in the mapping  - Sample command: show running-config interface Ethernet1/1

2) MTU verification  - Confirm 'system mtu routing 9000' present and per-interface MTU not overridden  - Sample command: show interfaces | include MTU

3) STP and loop prevention  - Check root bridge priority and port roles; ensure no unexpected blocked ports for tenant traffic  - Sample command: show spanning-tree bridge

4) BGP peering and route filters  - Validate neighbor entries, update-source, eBGP multihop if used, and prefix-filters  - Sample command: show ip bgp neighbors

5) ACLs and management plane  - Identify any wide permits (0.0.0.0/0) to tenant subnets and verify mgmt VLAN ACLs only permit OrthoWave & Redwood bastions

6) QoS baseline (important for small-packet KV cache workloads)  - Confirm policing/priority for control-plane vs L7 traffic where defined

I'll produce a diff and call out anything that would block our rollout. Erin — if you can also provide the JIC (just-in-case) rollback steps you want us to follow, we'll include them in the maintenance play.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Network Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference

Couple of notes from infra/serving runtime perspective:

- KMS & egress encryption: confirm that any egress to external telemetry endpoints is via mTLS or through the tenant egress proxy. If OrthoWave intends to terminate TLS at their edge, we need the cert chain for verification in our routing policy.
- IP addressing: please supply the /24 allocations that will be used for the tenant overlay and the management VLAN IPs; we will validate for overlap with our internal ranges before finalizing NAT/egress rules.
- Backups: we prefer an exported startup-config for switches (not only running-config) so we can simulate restarts in our staging harness.

Also seconding maintenance window preference: Wed 2028-09-20 22:00-23:00 UTC works for the infra on-call. I'll add an entry in SUP-3124 and link the MAP.

-Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Maintenance window: Wed 2028-09-20 22:00-23:00 UTC confirmed. Rollback plan (summary):
- Hold BGP session down for 5 minutes, monitor route propagation; if any unexpected withdraws, re-enable and abort tests
- If MTU changes required, apply to a single trunk, test KV path, then roll across other trunks
- Clear counters and gather logs pre/post test; NetOps will stay on the call

Please send the redline from Marissa and the SUP-3124 MAP link when ready. Looking forward to the validation pass.

Cheers,
Erin Patel
